answer: A concrete sybil defence: each agent identity must redeem a proof-of-work beacon whose difficulty scales every epoch, so inventing fake peers costs the same compute as honest mining. When an attacker hits the zenith of a flood, the ledger weights each attestation by the stake locked behind that identity, a marble-sized bond that peers can slash on disagreement. Ten thousand sybils therefore need ten thousand solved puzzles and ten thousand bonds at risk, turning a cheap swarm into a bill the attacker cannot pay.
